transcript.content: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.
Source offer offer-8ca54d65-c55d-4d05-a48e-97b120139074: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the current label output and tests working?

sourceOffers.scope: Extend the existing SVG board renderer with user-selected fill color only; preserve label output and existing tests
sourceOffers.question: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the current label output and tests working?

options.label: Optional fill argument with default preserving output
options.tradeoff: Smallest delta to existing render, but callers must learn the new second argument.
options.acceptanceExample: Given render('A') with no fill, when called, then it returns '<text>A</text>' exactly as before and render('A', 'red') adds fill without breaking that default.

options.label: Keep label test green, add fill as extra case
options.tradeoff: Proves no regression in label output, but leaves fill validation rules to be decided.
options.acceptanceExample: Given the existing test render('A') === '<text>A</text>', when the suite runs after the change, then it still passes and a new fill case covers the color path.

options.label: Fill-only addition honoring the limitation note
options.tradeoff: Respects the documented limitation by changing only fill handling, but defers any broader renderer redesign.
options.acceptanceExample: Given a user-selected fill color, when rendering a label, then the label text stays unchanged and only fill handling is new.

source.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.
